regressions.what: Large patches of grass have shifted from dark olive to pale yellow across the full clumps, overshooting the target on both banks.
The left soil face has changed from a dark undercut to a sunlit beige strip, losing the shadow directly beneath the sod.
The spring has lost most of its white falling water and now reflects as dark teal and black.

blockers.target: Olive-green clumps carry narrow golden highlights on upper blades and seed heads.
blockers.current: Pale yellow covers whole clumps, with the right-grass probe averaging 0.075 luminance above target.
blockers.change: Lower the right-bank vegetation mean by about 0.07 in normalized luminance and confine the brightest yellow to individual blade tips on both banks.

blockers.target: Broken blue-grey reflections cross the shallow water between and downstream of all three rocks with gravel visible through the gaps.
blockers.current: A blue band is visible on the lake, but the outlet changes abruptly to predominantly brown gravel.
blockers.change: Extend directional blue-grey ripple reflections through the outlet to the bottom edge and break them into short streaks that leave the gravel visible.

blockers.target: The left soil face sits in soft sod shadow while the shaded sides of the outlet rocks retain grey fracture detail.
blockers.current: The left face is pale and directly lit while the downstream face of the largest rock reads almost black.
blockers.change: Shade the left face under the turf lip and lift indirect light on the downstream rock faces enough to expose their fractures.

blockers.target: White aerated ribbons occupy the center of both drops with soft teal shadows and a pale reflection below.
blockers.current: Dark teal and black dominate the upper drop, with isolated white slashes on the lower drop.
blockers.change: Restore a broad white center to each drop, retain teal in the gaps and soften the reflected white below the inlet.

next.target: A projecting turf lip exposes a root curtain above a sloping soil face and partly buried rounded cobbles.
next.current: Straight exposed roots lie across a flat beige shelf terminating in a near-continuous line of angular stones.
next.change: Turn the roots downward below an irregular overhang, vary their hanging lengths and embed separated cobbles at the foot of the slope.

next.target: Tall irregular reed stands project into the water above a broad taper of overlapping grey pebbles and fist-sized stones.
next.current: Repeated radial grass tufts cover the bank above a shallow tan gravel strip with isolated large rocks.
next.change: Plant taller reeds in uneven waterside points and widen the exposed grey pebble ridge between those points.

next.target: Rounded fractured rock shoulders divide the flow into narrow white foam lines along both flanks.
next.current: The largest rock presents a steep angular face and the flank foam largely disappears into brown water.
next.change: Bevel the steep shoulders and wrap broken pale foam from upstream contact around each flank before trailing downstream.

excluded: Distant mountains and sky are outside this pass.
unverifiable: Water motion and vegetation movement cannot be judged from stills.
